hero.headline: US and Iran exchange air strikes in Gulf conflict
hero.body:
The United States and Iran conducted military strikes against each other around the Strait of Hormuz, according to reports from both governments. The latest exchange marks a continuation of escalating tensions in the region and raises questions about the stability of a ceasefire that appears fragile.

US Central Command forces shot down four Iranian attack drones that posed a threat around the strait. A ground control station in Iran's Bandar Abbas, which was preparing to launch a fifth drone, was also targeted in the strikes. A US official said the actions were "measured, purely defensive, and intended to maintain the ceasefire."

Two hours after the American strikes, Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded with an apparent retaliatory attack on an American air base in Kuwait. The Iranian state broadcaster claimed the base had "served as the source of the attack." Kuwait confirmed that its air defenses intercepted hostile missiles and drone threats early in the morning. American personnel were injured in the Iranian strike on Kuwaiti territory, marking a significant expansion of the conflict beyond direct US-Iran military installations.

The tit-for-tat strikes occurred as Iranian forces also fired at four ships attempting to cross the strait. Iran's state broadcaster reported the incident happened without coordination with security forces, though it provided no details about the vessels.

The exchange of strikes underscores how far apart the US and Iran remain in negotiations aimed at ending the war. Donald Trump has sent mixed signals about his approach, threatening to "finish the job" if Iran does not agree to a deal while also claiming both sides want to reach an agreement. "Either that or we'll have to just finish the job," Trump said at a White House cabinet meeting, adding that Iran was "negotiating on fumes."

Trump also appeared to direct a warning at Oman, a US ally, regarding potential arrangements for managing the Strait of Hormuz. He stated the waterway would be "open to everybody" and suggested Oman would need to cooperate or face consequences. The White House did not immediately clarify his remarks.

A key unresolved issue is whether a US-Iran ceasefire will cover Israel's operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Iran has insisted that Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire agreement with the United States. Meanwhile, Israel has intensified its military campaign in Lebanon, with the Israeli military striking over 550 targets since the beginning of the week. More than 1.2 million Lebanese have been displaced since March, and Israeli strikes have killed more than 3,200 people according to Lebanon's health ministry.

A US-brokered ceasefire announced in April now appears close to collapse, with fighting continuing despite the agreement. The escalating conflict continues to affect global oil markets and inflation concerns in the United States.

cards.headline: Macron urges Middle East leaders to support US-Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: The French president called for seizing an opportunity for a peace deal after months of war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron called on Middle East leaders to help the United States and Iran seize an opportunity for a peace deal following months of conflict that closed the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for global oil trade. Macron made his appeal after meeting with regional leaders including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, and Emirati officials.

According to reports, the Trump administration is seeking changes to any potential US-Iran agreement, with requested edits focusing on the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise 2% on Lebanon Conflict Expansion
cards.teaser: Israel's expanded offensive in Lebanon has reduced hopes for a ceasefire.
cards.body:
Oil markets responded sharply to escalating tensions in the Middle East. Brent crude futures jumped 2% as Israel expanded its offensive into Lebanon, undermining investor optimism about potential peace negotiations between the US and Iran.

The price movement reflects broader market volatility this month. Oil has experienced significant swings as traders weigh hopes for a ceasefire agreement against renewed regional conflict risks. The geopolitical uncertainty continues to drive energy market dynamics.

cards.headline: Daily pill doubles survival time for pancreatic cancer patients
cards.teaser: The drug daraxonrasib has been described as a breakthrough for the deadliest major cancer.
cards.body:
A daily pill called daraxonrasib has doubled survival time for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer, according to clinical trial results. Experts are calling it a "gamechanger" and one of the biggest breakthroughs in decades for treating the world's deadliest cancer.

Pancreatic cancer has historically had few effective treatments, with most doing little to help patients. The disease is often diagnosed late, after it has already spread to other parts of the body in more than half of cases. This breakthrough offers new hope for patients and their families facing this aggressive form of cancer.

cards.headline: Powell warns Federal Reserve credibility at risk in first remarks since leaving office
cards.body:
Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell has issued a stark warning that the central bank faces a critical credibility test, delivering the message during his first public remarks since stepping down from his position. Powell made the comments while accepting the John F. Kennedy Profiles in Courage award on Sunday evening.

Though Powell did not explicitly mention the Trump administration in his remarks, his warning clearly targeted recent efforts to undermine the Fed's independence from political pressure. He described the current moment as a stress test for the central bank, framing threats to its autonomy as a danger to an institution vital to American economic strength.

Powell's concerns reference several specific challenges facing the Fed. These include a criminal investigation into cost overruns on the central bank's headquarters renovation project and attempts by the Trump administration to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook from her position. Powell characterized the investigation into the building renovation as a pretext for pressuring the central bank to lower interest rates.

The Federal Reserve operates as an independent agency responsible for setting monetary policy and interest rates without direct government interference. This independence has long been considered essential to effective economic management and protecting the institution from short-term political manipulation.

Powell's term as chair ended on May 15, when Kevin Warsh officially took over leadership of the central bank following his Senate confirmation on May 14. The confirmation vote was highly contentious, passing 54-45 along party lines with one exception. Democratic Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania joined the Republican majority in supporting Warsh's appointment. The vote marked the most divisive confirmation for a Fed chair in history.

Warsh, a 54-year-old economist and former Wall Street banker who previously served as a Fed governor from 2006 to 2011, will lead the central bank during a period of intense scrutiny over its independence. The Trump administration has pressed the Fed to lower interest rates despite inflation currently standing at 3.8 percent. Critics, including Senator Elizabeth Warren, have expressed concern that Warsh will function as Trump's "sock puppet" in controlling monetary policy decisions.

During his Senate banking committee hearing, Warsh pledged to maintain Fed independence and remove politics from monetary policy. However, he declined to answer questions about whether Trump lost the 2020 election, raising alarms among Democrats about his commitment to institutional norms.

Powell announced last month that he would remain on the Fed board as a voting governor rather than retiring after his chair term concluded. He indicated he would stay in this position until the Trump administration ends its scrutiny of the Fed's renovation project.

cards.headline: UAW calls midnight strike at American Axle plant supplying GM trucks
cards.teaser: The United Auto Workers union launched a strike at a key General Motors supplier as contract negotiations reached a deadline.
cards.body:
The UAW declared a strike at American Axle starting at midnight as the union's contract deadline approached. The plant supplies critical components for General Motors pickup trucks, potentially disrupting production of one of the automaker's most profitable vehicle lines.

The strike at American Axle represents the latest labor action in the automotive sector. Workers at the facility produce axles and other drivetrain parts essential to GM's truck manufacturing operations. The walkout could affect vehicle assembly if the strike extends for more than a few days.

hero.headline: Blast Kills Dozens in Rebel-Held Myanmar Village
hero.teaser: Insurgents attribute the explosion to mining explosives near the Chinese border.
hero.body:
A massive explosion in a Myanmar village controlled by insurgent forces has killed dozens of people. The village is located near the border with China.

According to rebel groups in the area, the blast resulted from explosives used in mining operations. The incident represents one of the deadliest single events in Myanmar's ongoing civil conflict.

cards.headline: Nicaraguan Indigenous Leader Brooklyn Rivera Dies in Government Custody
cards.teaser: The Miskito political leader was arrested by the government in 2023.
cards.body:
Brooklyn Rivera, a prominent Miskito political leader, died at age 73 following his arrest by Nicaraguan authorities in 2023. He had been held in government custody for nearly three years.

Rights groups have condemned both his prolonged detention and the circumstances of his death, characterizing his imprisonment as arbitrary. His family disputes the government's official account of what led to his death.

cards.headline: Israel Captures Historic Castle in Southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: The seizure of Beaufort recalls memories of Israel's previous occupation of Lebanese territory.
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort, a 12th-century castle in southern Lebanon that overlooks the border with northern Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the seizure as a "decisive shift" in Israel's campaign against Hezbollah, suggesting the military plans an extended presence in the region.

The capture carries significant symbolic weight, evoking memories of Israel's previous occupation of southern Lebanon from 1982 to 2000. The offensive has drawn criticism from European governments concerned about escalation. Oil prices jumped 2% following the expanded military operations, raising questions about prospects for a ceasefire.

cards.headline: Colombia Presidential Election Goes to Runoff
cards.teaser: Abelardo de la Espriella will face leftist senator Iván Cepeda in a June runoff.
cards.body:
Colombia will hold a runoff presidential election on June 21 after no candidate won a majority in the first round. Left-wing senator Iván Cepeda, backed by outgoing President Gustavo Petro's party, will face Abelardo de la Espriella, a Trump admirer.

The election serves as a referendum on Petro's policies as Colombia navigates its future a decade after signing a historic peace agreement with the FARC guerrilla group. The runoff outcome could significantly reshape Colombia's relationship with the United States and determine the country's direction on domestic and peace-related issues.

cards.headline: Two American Commentators Banned From Entering UK
cards.teaser: Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur were barred from entering the United Kingdom.
cards.body:
British authorities banned Hasan Piker, a political livestreamer, and Cenk Uygur, founder of The Young Turks news program, from entering the United Kingdom. Both are American political commentators with substantial online followings.

Members of Parliament had urged the Home Office to revoke Piker's visa ahead of a planned speech in London. Piker said the UK barred him and criticized what he called the power of pro-Israel groups in the decision.

cards.headline: Poland Restores Highway Bus Route Numbered 666
cards.teaser: The service to the seaside resort of Hel returns despite earlier objections from Christian organizations.
cards.body:
Poland's seaside resort town of Hel is restoring its bus route numbered 666. The service had previously drawn objections from Christian groups concerned about the number's biblical associations.

Transportation authorities have decided to reintroduce the numbered route despite the earlier controversy, bringing back the service to the coastal destination.

cards.headline: 2025 Wildfires Set Cost Record
cards.teaser: Researchers say blazes in densely populated areas drove the year's losses.
cards.body:
Wildfires in 2025 were the costliest on record, according to researchers. The severe financial toll resulted from hard-to-control blazes that burned through densely populated regions.

Fires in areas like Los Angeles were particularly destructive and difficult to contain. The combination of severe fire conditions and proximity to residential and commercial areas drove the record losses for the year.

cards.headline: Satellite images show Iranian strikes damaged 20 US military sites
cards.teaser: Analysts say Tehran's attacks on American facilities have been more extensive than publicly acknowledged.
cards.body:
Satellite imagery reviewed by BBC Verify has documented damage to 20 US military sites from Iranian attacks since the war began. The visual evidence provides an independent assessment of the extent of Tehran's strikes against American military infrastructure in the region.

Analysts who examined the satellite data told BBC Verify that Iran's strikes were more extensive than what US officials had publicly acknowledged. The documentation offers concrete evidence of damage inflicted on US military facilities during the conflict.

cards.headline: Americans injured in Iranian missile strike on Kuwait air base
cards.teaser: Tehran launched missiles and drones at a Kuwaiti facility hosting US personnel.
cards.body:
American personnel were injured when Iran launched a missile and drone attack on an air base in Kuwait. The strike targeted a facility that hosts US military forces, expanding the conflict to include attacks on American troops stationed in allied nations.

Kuwait reported that its air defenses opened fire to intercept the incoming drones and missiles. US officials described the Iranian attack as a ceasefire violation, though the terms and status of any truce have not been detailed in available reports.

cards.headline: Senate Democrat Graham Platner faces scrutiny over sexual messages
cards.teaser: Reports say the candidate's wife flagged sexually explicit texts to his campaign.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Democratic Senate candidate in Maine, is facing fallout after reports that his wife flagged sexually explicit messages he sent to other women. The revelations have prompted concern from fellow Democrats, including US Senator Cory Booker, who said Platner "has questions to answer."

Booker expressed his concerns publicly on ABC's This Week, suggesting the campaign process would be an appropriate venue for addressing the allegations. The controversy has complicated Democratic efforts in the competitive Senate race.

cards.headline: Georgia towns use novel legal strategy to fight ICE detention facility
cards.teaser: Small communities are challenging federal immigration plans in a way legal experts find noteworthy.
cards.body:
Social Circle, a small Georgia town of about 5,000 residents, has filed a federal lawsuit against plans to convert a warehouse into a large ICE detention facility. Rather than relying on standard environmental arguments, the town is invoking state "public nuisance" law, claiming the facility would harm residents' health, safety, and wellbeing.

Legal experts say this novel approach could reshape how local governments challenge federal immigration enforcement infrastructure. The lawsuit goes beyond other recent challenges that focus on federal environmental assessment requirements, potentially creating a wider impact for other communities facing similar proposals.

cards.headline: Athlete wins $149,000 tribunal after 800-mile trip to meet absent boss
cards.teaser: Beth Littlewood says the case could help thousands after she drove from Germany for a meeting her supervisor skipped.
cards.body:
Beth Littlewood has won a tribunal award of $149,000 after she was forced to drive 800 miles from Germany for a meeting that her boss did not attend. The athlete described the incident as the final straw in her employment dispute.

Littlewood said the tribunal decision could help thousands of other workers facing similar situations. The case centered on the requirement that she travel such a significant distance for work obligations that were not honored by her employer.

hero.headline: Berkshire Hathaway acquires homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion
hero.body:
Berkshire Hathaway has agreed to purchase homebuilder Taylor Morrison in a deal valued at $6.8 billion, or $8.5 billion when including the company's assumed debt. The acquisition marks the first major deal under newly announced CEO Greg Abel, signaling his willingness to pursue large-scale transactions as he prepares to take over the conglomerate at year-end 2025.

Warren Buffett revealed his retirement plans at Berkshire's annual shareholder meeting, announcing that Abel will become CEO when Buffett steps down after leading the company for 60 years. "I think the time has arrived where Greg should become the chief executive officer of the company at year end," Buffett told thousands of investors gathered in Omaha, Nebraska. The announcement surprised many, as Buffett had previously insisted he had no plans to retire. The crowd responded with a lengthy standing ovation.

Abel, 62, has served as Berkshire's vice chairman and has been the designated successor since 2001. As a 25-year veteran of the company, he already oversees all non-insurance operations, managing dozens of businesses spanning fossil energy, chemicals, real estate, and retail. The Taylor Morrison acquisition demonstrates Abel's approach to deploying Berkshire's substantial cash reserves into sectors aligned with the conglomerate's existing interests.

The homebuilder operates as a national builder with projects across multiple states. Under Berkshire's ownership, Taylor Morrison is expected to maintain operational independence while accessing the parent company's financial resources. The transaction requires regulatory approval and is projected to close later this year.

The deal reflects confidence in residential construction demand despite economic uncertainties. Berkshire has previously invested in housing-related sectors, including building materials and manufactured homes, making this acquisition a natural extension of the company's portfolio.

Buffett also addressed broader economic concerns during the shareholder meeting. He warned about the consequences of tariff policies, stating that "there's no question that trade can be an act of war." He criticized trade restrictions for creating global instability and damaging international relationships. "We should be looking to trade with the rest of the world. We should do what we do best and they should do what they do best," Buffett said.

In February, Berkshire reported record annual operating profits of $47.44 billion in 2024, representing a 27 percent increase. The company operates 189 businesses, and the impact of current trade policies on these operations remains unclear.

Buffett reiterated his long-term commitment to Berkshire, saying he has "zero" intention of selling shares. He plans to eventually donate 99.5 percent of his wealth to charitable causes through a trust managed by his children. According to Forbes, his current net worth stands at $165.3 billion.

cards.headline: UAW calls midnight strike at American Axle plant supplying GM trucks
cards.teaser: The United Auto Workers union launched a strike at a key General Motors supplier as contract negotiations reached a deadline.
cards.body:
The UAW declared a strike at American Axle starting at midnight as the union's contract deadline approached. The plant supplies critical components for General Motors pickup trucks, potentially disrupting production of one of the automaker's most profitable vehicle lines.

The strike at American Axle represents the latest labor action in the automotive sector. Workers at the facility produce axles and other drivetrain parts essential to GM's truck manufacturing operations. The walkout could affect vehicle assembly if the strike extends for more than a few days.

cards.headline: Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell warns Fed credibility at risk
cards.teaser: Powell cautioned that political pressure threatens the Federal Reserve's independence and public trust.
cards.body:
Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell issued a pointed warning about threats to the central bank's credibility amid ongoing political attacks. Powell, who left the Fed earlier this year, accepted the JFK Profile in Courage award while delivering his message wrapped in abstract language about institutional independence.

The former chair suggested the Fed faces a stress test as it navigates political pressure. His comments come as the central bank continues managing inflation and interest rate policy. Powell's tenure ended earlier in 2026 after years of tension between the Fed and political leaders over monetary policy decisions.

cards.headline: Bond market signals new inflation concerns ahead of midterm elections
cards.teaser: Rising bond yields point to investor worries about inflation, creating political challenges for the administration.
cards.body:
The bond market is flashing warnings about inflation as midterm elections approach, adding pressure to the current political landscape. Bond yields have risen as investors reassess inflation expectations, suggesting concern about the trajectory of prices despite earlier optimism.

The inflation dynamics present a political risk heading into the midterms. Economic messaging around inflation helped shape the previous election cycle, and renewed price pressures could influence voter sentiment. Republican lawmakers face particular challenges as they navigate constituent concerns about cost of living increases.

cards.headline: Nvidia unveils AI chip designed for personal computers
cards.teaser: The technology company introduced new hardware aimed at bringing artificial intelligence capabilities to consumer PCs.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced a new AI chip specifically designed for personal computers. CEO Jensen Huang described the product launch as the reinvention of the computer, positioning the chip as a transformative addition to consumer hardware.

The new processor represents Nvidia's push to expand AI capabilities beyond data centers and into everyday computing devices. The chip aims to enable AI-powered applications to run directly on personal computers rather than relying on cloud processing. Nvidia has dominated the market for AI training chips used in large-scale data centers.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO scheduled for June 12 reshapes Wall Street expectations
cards.teaser: The space company's public offering forces investment banks to reorganize around what could be one of the largest tech listings.
cards.body:
SpaceX's June 12 IPO is reshaping Wall Street operations as the space company prepares for its market debut. The offering comes after SpaceX secured $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts, underscoring the company's role in government spaceflight operations. According to its IPO filing, government contracts already represent one-fifth of SpaceX's 2025 revenue.

The IPO is expected to test the current stock market rally, with investment banks reorganizing to handle the anticipated launch. SpaceX's dominance in commercial spaceflight through Starlink's satellite network and reusable rocket technology positions the company as a major player in both the space industry and public markets.

cards.headline: Horror film Backrooms earns $82 million on $10 million budget
cards.teaser: Young moviegoers drove ticket sales for the low-budget horror film from a 20-year-old filmmaker.
cards.body:
The horror film Backrooms generated $82 million in ticket sales despite a production budget of just $10 million. The movie came from a 20-year-old filmmaker and attracted young audiences willing to visit theaters for compelling content.

The box office performance adds evidence that younger demographics will attend theatrical releases when offerings match their interests. The film's success ratio of more than eight times its production cost demonstrates the continued viability of theatrical distribution for genre films that connect with specific audience segments.

hero.headline: NVIDIA Launches Arm-Based AI Chip for Personal Computers
hero.body:
NVIDIA announced a new chip designed to bring artificial intelligence capabilities to personal computers, marking its first entry into the PC processor market. The company unveiled the Arm-based processor in partnership with Microsoft, with laptops from Dell and HP also planned to use the chip.

Microsoft introduced the Surface Laptop Ultra as the first device featuring the new NVIDIA processor. The collaboration between NVIDIA and Microsoft aims to integrate AI processing directly into Windows PCs, allowing users to run AI applications locally rather than relying on cloud-based services. The chip architecture uses Arm technology, the same instruction set used in most smartphones, rather than the x86 architecture that has dominated PCs for decades.

The move puts NVIDIA in direct competition with Intel and AMD in the PC processor market. NVIDIA has been the dominant supplier of graphics processors for AI data centers, but this represents its expansion into consumer computing. The company has positioned the chips as purpose-built for what it calls the age of personal AI, suggesting capabilities for running AI agents and applications on individual devices.

Major PC manufacturers have committed to using the new processors. Dell and HP plan to release laptops with the NVIDIA chip, joining Microsoft in the initial product lineup. The announcements indicate a broader industry shift toward incorporating dedicated AI processing hardware into consumer devices.

The timing of the launch follows growing demand for AI capabilities in consumer technology. Tech companies have been racing to integrate AI features into their products, but most current implementations require cloud connectivity and remote servers. Local AI processing could enable faster response times and better privacy by keeping data on the user's device. The success of the new chips will depend on software support, pricing, and whether the AI features prove valuable enough to consumers to justify switching from established Intel and AMD processors.

cards.headline: Meteor Explodes Over Massachusetts With Force of 300 Tons of TNT
cards.teaser: NASA confirmed a meteor explosion over New England caused loud booms and shaking across multiple states.
cards.body:
A meteor detonated over Massachusetts with an explosive force equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, causing widespread shaking across Southern New England. NASA confirmed the meteor was responsible for the loud booms that residents reported hearing throughout the region.

Sightings and reports of the explosion extended across a large area, from Delaware to Montreal. The incident prompted numerous calls to authorities from residents who felt the tremors and heard the mysterious sounds.

cards.headline: Dell Launches $699 XPS 13 Laptop to Compete With Apple MacBook Neo
cards.teaser: Dell unveiled a touchscreen XPS 13 laptop priced at $699, positioning it against Apple's MacBook Neo.
cards.body:
Dell has announced a new XPS 13 laptop designed to challenge Apple's MacBook Neo in the budget segment. The device features a touchscreen and launches in July with a promotional student price of $599 through September. After the back-to-school promotion ends, the laptop will cost $699.

The XPS 13 represents Dell's return to the product line as an affordable alternative to Apple's entry-level MacBook. The promotional pricing undercuts Apple's offering during the critical back-to-school shopping season.

cards.headline: AMD Reintroduces Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU to Address RAM Costs
cards.teaser: AMD announced it will bring back the Ryzen 7 5800X3D processor and introduce a new 7700X3D model.
cards.body:
AMD formally announced the Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition and the Ryzen 7 7700X3D as part of its strategy to provide options for users facing high RAM costs. The 5800X3D will be priced at $349, while the 7700X3D is set at $329.

The move revives the Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU to celebrate 10 years of the AM4 platform. AMD's pitch centers on the continued viability of older technology, allowing users to avoid upgrading to newer platforms that require more expensive RAM. The Verge described the strategy as AMD promoting its old technology as still good enough for current use.

cards.headline: Alienware Releases First 39-Inch 5K OLED Monitor With RGB Stripe Panel
cards.teaser: Dell's gaming brand unveiled the AW3926QW, marking the first 39-inch 5K OLED monitor using RGB stripe technology.
cards.body:
Alienware unveiled the AW3926QW at Computex 2026, marking the world's first 39-inch 5K OLED monitor featuring an RGB stripe panel. The monitor succeeds Alienware's original QD-OLED gaming monitor from 2022, delivering an upgraded design and enhanced specifications.

The announcement is part of Alienware's 30th anniversary celebration, which includes a broader lineup of gaming monitors exceeding 30 inches. Alongside the flagship 39-inch model, the company also introduced a 34-inch OLED gaming monitor.

cards.headline: Artist KC Green Settles Dispute With AI Startup Over 'This Is Fine' Meme
cards.teaser: KC Green, creator of the 'This is fine' meme, reached an agreement with AI startup Artisan.
cards.body:
KC Green, the artist behind the widely used 'This is fine' meme, reached an agreement with AI startup Artisan. The startup has taken down advertisements that used the meme.

The resolution follows a dispute over Artisan's use of Green's artwork in its marketing materials. The agreement ends the conflict between the artist and the AI company over the unauthorized commercial use of the popular internet meme.

cards.headline: Environmental Activist Erin Brockovich Targets Data Center Secrecy
cards.teaser: Erin Brockovich has focused her environmental activism on data center transparency issues.
cards.body:
Environmental activist Erin Brockovich has made data center secrecy her new mission. The activist, known for her work on environmental contamination cases, is now taking aim at the lack of transparency surrounding data center operations.

Brockovich's campaign addresses concerns about the environmental impact and operational practices of data centers. The focus represents a shift in her activism toward

hero.headline: Spurs and Knicks to meet in NBA Finals rematch 27 years after 1999 championship
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs will face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, reuniting two franchises that last met for the championship in 1999. The Spurs advanced by defeating the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night, while the Knicks secured their spot through the Eastern Conference playoffs. Game 1 is scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs' charge against the defending champion Thunder. The 7-foot-4 French player finished with 22 points and seven rebounds while earning series MVP honors. However, Wembanyama emphasized his teammates' contributions to the victory. Julian Champagnie scored 20 points including six three-pointers, Dylan Harper made an impact off the bench, and backup center Luke Kornet delivered a crucial block in the fourth quarter as Oklahoma City mounted a comeback attempt.

The Thunder, playing without Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury, struggled to keep pace as the final moments approached. Reigning NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 35 points with nine assists but received limited offensive support from his teammates, as no other Thunder player reached 20 points.

Wembanyama became emotional after securing the Finals berth. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," the 22-year-old explained when asked about his tears. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

Champagnie reflected on the team's confidence heading into the Finals. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said following the game.

Thunder coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the difficult loss while maintaining perspective. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he stated. "And it's the NBA—there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The 1999 Finals between these same franchises ended with the Spurs winning the series 4-1 to capture their first championship in franchise history. Tim Duncan earned Finals MVP in that matchup. The Knicks reached the Finals that year as the eighth seed in the Eastern Conference. This upcoming Finals represents a significant return to prominence for New York, which has not appeared in the championship round since that 1999 loss. For San Antonio, the appearance continues the franchise's tradition of postseason success across multiple generations of players.

cards.headline: US men's soccer team defeats Senegal 3-2 in World Cup preparation match
cards.teaser: Christian Pulisic scored as the United States beat Senegal in a pre-tournament friendly in Charlotte.
cards.body:
Christian Pulisic ended a nearly six-month goal drought Sunday, leading the United States to a 3-2 victory over Senegal in Charlotte, North Carolina. Pulisic both assisted on the opening goal and scored himself in the first half as the Americans dominated early. Sergiño Dest opened the scoring just seven minutes in, giving the US an early advantage in their World Cup preparations.

Senegal mounted a comeback with Sadio Mané scoring twice to make it close, but the US held on for the win. The match served as an important tuneup before the Americans face Germany on June 6 in Chicago in their final friendly before the World Cup.

cards.headline: Illinois lawmakers craft new stadium proposal to keep Bears from leaving state
cards.teaser: State legislators developed a revised plan centered on a publicly owned stadium as a midnight deadline approached.
cards.body:
Illinois lawmakers worked on a compromise stadium bill aimed at preventing the Chicago Bears from relocating out of state. The new proposal centers on a publicly owned stadium structure and was crafted as an amendment to House Bill 958 after an earlier megaprojects bill failed to gain traction.

The Senate filed the compromise legislation as lawmakers raced to meet a midnight deadline. NBC Chicago characterized the effort as a plan B strategy. Multiple outlets reported that the revised approach represents a fourth-down attempt to save stadium financing legislation after previous proposals stalled in the General Assembly.

cards.headline: 19-year-old Joao Fonseca advances to French Open quarterfinals
cards.teaser: The rising Brazilian tennis player defeated two-time finalist Casper Ruud to reach the tournament's final eight.
cards.body:
Joao Fonseca advanced to the French Open quarterfinals with a victory over Casper Ruud, the two-time finalist from Norway. The 19-year-old Brazilian has now backed up his earlier win against Novak Djokovic, demonstrating his credentials as a title contender at Roland Garros.

The match was overshadowed by controversy involving a line-call ruling on the clay court. With all previous French Open champions eliminated from both the men's and women's draws, the tournament is wide open for new champions to emerge.

cards.headline: North Carolina baseball defeats East Carolina 9-3 to reach Super Regional
cards.teaser: The Tar Heels advanced to their 13th Super Regional after winning the Chapel Hill regional tournament.
cards.body:
The University of North Carolina baseball team defeated East Carolina 9-3 in the regional final to advance to the Super Regional round of the NCAA tournament. The victory marked the 13th time the Tar Heels have reached the Super Regional stage in program history.

East Carolina entered the game seeking to stave off elimination after dropping into the loser's bracket. The Pirates had previously defeated VCU 10-0 to reach the regional final. North Carolina's nine-run performance ended ECU's tournament run and kept the Tar Heels' College World Series hopes alive.

cards.headline: Georgia baseball player Tre Phelps suspended after ejection in win over Liberty
cards.teaser: The player will miss the next game following his removal from the field during a home run celebration.
cards.body:
Georgia baseball player Tre Phelps will sit out the Bulldogs' next game after being ejected during a regional tournament victory over Liberty. Phelps and head coach Wes Johnson were both removed from the game following a home run celebration that officials deemed excessive.

Georgia defeated Liberty 6-2 to advance to the NCAA Athens Regional final. The ejection and subsequent one-game suspension sparked discussion about enforcement of celebration rules in college baseball. Georgia advanced to the Super Regional round despite the controversy surrounding the ejection.

cards.headline: Oregon baseball advances to Super Regional with win over Oregon State
cards.teaser: The Ducks defeated their in-state rival in the Eugene Regional final to continue their tournament run.
cards.body:
Oregon defeated Oregon State in the Eugene Regional final to advance to the Super Regional round of the NCAA baseball tournament. Pitcher Sanford delivered a strong performance to lead the Ducks to victory in the rivalry matchup.

The game completed the Eugene Regional bracket and sent Oregon through to the next round. Oregon State entered the regional final after defeating Washington State earlier in the tournament. The Register-Guard and other Oregon

hero.headline: Matt Brown, Alaskan Bush People star, found dead in Washington river at 42
hero.body:
Matt Brown, a star of the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, was found dead in a Washington state river. He was 42 years old. His family confirmed his death, and according to reports, his brother Noah helped pull his body from the water.

Brown appeared on Alaskan Bush People, a reality show that followed the Brown family as they lived in remote areas of Alaska and later Washington state. The series premiered in 2014 and ran for multiple seasons, documenting the family's off-the-grid lifestyle. Matt Brown was one of seven siblings featured on the show alongside their parents.

The Discovery Channel show gained a substantial following over its run, making the Brown family recognizable figures in reality television. Matt Brown's appearances on the series spanned several years before he stepped back from regular participation in later seasons. The show continued production even after the death of the family patriarch, Billy Brown, in 2021.

The circumstances surrounding his death have not been detailed in official statements. His body was recovered from a river in Washington state, where the family had relocated in recent years after spending time in Alaska. Noah Brown, one of Matt's brothers and a fellow cast member, was involved in the recovery efforts.

The Brown family released a statement confirming Matt's death but did not provide additional details about the timeline or cause. The family has experienced significant losses in recent years, including the death of their father. Matt Brown leaves behind his mother, Ami Brown, and his siblings, several of whom continue to appear in various media projects related to their family's story.

cards.headline: Euphoria ends with season 3, HBO confirms
cards.teaser: The HBO drama series Euphoria has concluded after seven years, three seasons, and 26 episodes.
cards.body:
Creator, writer, and director Sam Levinson announced the end of Euphoria on the New York Times music podcast Popcast. HBO confirmed the announcement to media outlets. The series ran for seven years across three seasons with 26 total episodes.

The show, which premiered in 2019, starred Zendaya as Rue Bennett and became one of HBO's most talked-about dramas. The season 3 finale included a major death among the ensemble cast, though some core characters received limited screen time in the final episode.

cards.headline: Euphoria finale kills off main character Rue Bennett
cards.teaser: The final episode of Euphoria ended with the death of Rue Bennett, played by Zendaya, at the hands of drug dealer Alamo.
cards.body:
The Season 3 finale of Euphoria, titled In God We Trust, featured the death of protagonist Rue Bennett. Actor Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje, who played drug dealer Alamo Brown, explained his character's motivation for killing Rue in interviews following the episode's release on HBO Max.

The finale also included limited screen time for several core characters and concluded storylines for other members of the ensemble cast. Colman Domingo, who played Ali, appeared in the final scenes of the episode. The finale brought resolution to the series after three seasons.

cards.headline: Backrooms earns $82 million in opening weekend box office
cards.teaser: The horror film Backrooms debuted with $81 million to $82 million in ticket sales, powered by young moviegoers.
cards.body:
Backrooms, a horror film, opened with between $81 million and $82 million at the domestic box office, exceeding industry expectations. The film drew a significant audience of younger viewers, according to box office analysts and reports.

The film's debut represents a shift in Hollywood, as it was created by filmmakers with backgrounds in YouTube content creation. The opening weekend performance outpaced projections and set records for films produced by content creators transitioning to traditional theatrical releases. The success comes as other major releases experienced significant drops in their second weekends.

cards.headline: John Oliver criticizes Trump's Freedom 250 concert series
cards.teaser: Comedian John Oliver devoted the opening of his HBO show to criticism of President Trump's Freedom 250 concert lineup.
cards.body:
John Oliver used the opening segment of Last Week Tonight to critique President Trump's Freedom 250 concert series, which aims to celebrate America's 250th birthday. Oliver joined fellow HBO host Bill Maher in commenting on the event.

The concert series experienced significant performer withdrawals, with artists including country singer Martina McBride, Young MC, and Poison frontman Bret Michaels dropping out due to concerns about the event's political nature. Following the departures, Trump attacked the withdrawing artists and suggested he might hold a MAGA rally instead of the concert at the planned Great American State Fair in Washington, D.C.

cards.headline: M.I.A. sues Kid Cudi for $2.8 million over tour removal
cards.teaser: Rapper M.I.A. filed a lawsuit against Kid Cudi for $2.8 million after being removed from his Rebel Ragers Tour.
cards.body:
M.I.A. was removed from Kid Cudi's Rebel Ragers Tour after making remarks during her opening act that Kid Cudi characterized as offensive. The British rapper responded by filing a $2.8 million lawsuit against the headliner.

In a statement, M.I.A.'s team said Kid Cudi's attempts to silence freedom of artistic expression and speech on his tour could not go unchallenged. Kid Cudi claimed the decision to remove M.I.A. from the tour was based on her comments during performances. The legal action centers on the financial impact of her removal from the tour dates.

cards.headline: DirecTV drops 54 Scripps local stations in 36 markets
cards.teaser: A contract dispute between DirecTV and Scripps resulted in 54 local television stations going dark across 36 markets.
cards.body:
Scripps and DirecTV failed to reach a retransmission agreement, leading to a blackout of 54 Scripps-owned local stations in 36 Nielsen-designated markets starting at 7 p.m. ET. Both companies blamed each other for the failure to reach a deal.

DirecTV noted the blackout's timing comes ahead of several state and local primary elections scheduled for June, as well as upcoming NBA playoffs. The affected stations include local affiliates in markets across the country

hero.headline: Powell warns Federal Reserve credibility at risk in first remarks since leaving office
hero.body:
Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell has issued a stark warning that the central bank faces a critical credibility test, delivering the message during his first public remarks since stepping down from his position. Powell made the comments while accepting the John F. Kennedy Profiles in Courage award on Sunday evening.

Though Powell did not explicitly mention the Trump administration in his remarks, his warning clearly targeted recent efforts to undermine the Fed's independence from political pressure. He described the current moment as a stress test for the central bank, framing threats to its autonomy as a danger to an institution vital to American economic strength.

Powell's concerns reference several specific challenges facing the Fed. These include a criminal investigation into cost overruns on the central bank's headquarters renovation project and attempts by the Trump administration to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook from her position. Powell characterized the investigation into the building renovation as a pretext for pressuring the central bank to lower interest rates.

The Federal Reserve operates as an independent agency responsible for setting monetary policy and interest rates without direct government interference. This independence has long been considered essential to effective economic management and protecting the institution from short-term political manipulation.

Powell's term as chair ended on May 15, when Kevin Warsh officially took over leadership of the central bank following his Senate confirmation on May 14. The confirmation vote was highly contentious, passing 54-45 along party lines with one exception. Democratic Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania joined the Republican majority in supporting Warsh's appointment. The vote marked the most divisive confirmation for a Fed chair in history.

Warsh, a 54-year-old economist and former Wall Street banker who previously served as a Fed governor from 2006 to 2011, will lead the central bank during a period of intense scrutiny over its independence. The Trump administration has pressed the Fed to lower interest rates despite inflation currently standing at 3.8 percent. Critics, including Senator Elizabeth Warren, have expressed concern that Warsh will function as Trump's "sock puppet" in controlling monetary policy decisions.

During his Senate banking committee hearing, Warsh pledged to maintain Fed independence and remove politics from monetary policy. However, he declined to answer questions about whether Trump lost the 2020 election, raising alarms among Democrats about his commitment to institutional norms.

Powell announced last month that he would remain on the Fed board as a voting governor rather than retiring after his chair term concluded. He indicated he would stay in this position until the Trump administration ends its scrutiny of the Fed's renovation project.

cards.headline: Pence criticizes Trump for abandoning conservative principles
cards.teaser: The former vice president wrote that Trump has shifted toward populist policies and away from his conservative base.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized President Trump in a Wall Street Journal opinion piece, arguing that Trump has abandoned conservative principles for populist policies. Pence described a shift in Trump's rhetoric and tone that now emphasizes widespread reform through populist measures.

Pence also referenced Trump's actions regarding him during the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot. The former vice president served under Trump from 2017 to 2021 before their public split over the events surrounding the certification of the 2020 election results.

cards.headline: Ken Paxton to meet Senate leader after defeating John Cornyn in GOP primary
cards.teaser: The Texas attorney general beat the four-term senator in a runoff election for the Republican Senate nomination.
cards.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said he will meet with Senate Majority Leader John Thune after winning the Republican primary runoff to replace Senator John Cornyn. Paxton defeated Cornyn, who has served four terms in the Senate.

Paxton said he has been in contact with Thune, Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, and Republican Conference Chair Tom Cotton since his victory. The meetings signal Paxton's preparation for a potential transition to the Senate if he wins the general election.

cards.headline: Trump defends departure of 10,000 government lawyers as positive development
cards.teaser: The president responded to a New York Times report on the exodus of legal staff from federal agencies.
cards.body:
President Trump said the departure of thousands of lawyers from the federal government is positive, responding to a New York Times report on the staff exodus. The Times reported that more than 10,000 lawyers working for the federal government left their positions between the end of 2024 and March.

Trump characterized the departures as beneficial for his administration. The exodus represents a substantial reduction in the federal government's legal workforce across multiple agencies during the first months of Trump's current term.

cards.headline: Macron urges Middle East leaders to support US-Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: The French president called for seizing an opportunity for a peace deal after months of war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron called on Middle East leaders to help the United States and Iran seize an opportunity for a peace deal following months of conflict that closed the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for global oil trade. Macron made his appeal after meeting with regional leaders including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, and Emirati officials.

According to reports, the Trump administration is seeking changes to any potential US-Iran agreement, with requested edits focusing on the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium.

cards.headline: New Jersey resumes family visits at detention center after protests
cards.teaser: Governor Mikie Sherrill said limited visitation would restart at the Newark facility following demonstrations over conditions.
cards.body:
Family visitation has been restored at Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark following a week of protests, Governor Mikie Sherrill and the Department of Homeland Security announced Sunday.

Visits were suspended after detainees began a hunger strike, sparking heated demonstrations outside the facility. The resumption comes as families seek clarity on which detainees will be allowed visitors. Local officials have also imposed an indefinite overnight curfew beginning at 9 p.m. in the blocked-off area surrounding the detention center.

cards.headline: Democratic Party chair faces pressure over 2024 election review and finances
cards.teaser: DNC Chair Ken Martin is confronting internal criticism as the party sets its 2028 presidential primary calendar.
cards.body:
Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin faces growing criticism from party members over the committee's review of the 2024 election and its financial struggles. The dispute represents the most significant early test of Democratic leadership heading into the 2028 election cycle.

Martin has so far prevented a revolt among DNC members as they work to set the calendar for the 2028 presidential primary. Critics have questioned both the committee's analysis of what went wrong in 2024 and its current financial position under Martin's leadership.
